knowledge.title: Filter without fetching
knowledge.prompt: Choose To do, open the overview, then open the walk’s notes.
knowledge.explanation: Filtering and the overview reuse the task list. Opening notes asks for a missing field, so it reads once more. Returning to that detail reuses the new information.

results.title: When part of the list is missing
results.prompt: Choose what the task service returns.
results.explanation: A missing title keeps the matching task visible. A missing filter status leaves a candidate unresolved. A failed read preserves known tasks and offers retry. Only complete empty membership proves that there are no tasks.

actions.title: A checkmark before confirmation
actions.prompt: Complete the walk, then let the task service reply.
actions.explanation: A command proposes a completed task while its action awaits a reply. Confirm, reject, save only a note, or lose the reply. Only confirmed success establishes completion; an unknown outcome keeps the preview unconfirmed.

editor.title: Keep your own draft
editor.prompt: Change the meeting time and save the task.
editor.explanation: A managed edit keeps your input with the version it came from. A teammate’s change does not replace your draft. Saving against that older version conflicts. Read-only access keeps readable input; losing notes access removes just the private notes.

access.title: Who can still read the notes?
access.prompt: Turn off Team access, then the direct invitation.
access.explanation: Either permission can disclose the same private note. Losing both removes the note while the public task survives. A reply captured before withdrawal cannot restore that note after regrant; a new authorized update can.

recovery.title: Return to an unfinished action
recovery.prompt: Complete the walk, then close and reopen the example.
recovery.explanation: The first owner records possible submission and sends once. A replacement owner restores its journal and investigates. Missing confirmation leaves the result unknown; recovery never resubmits the command.

planning.title: One plan for several views
planning.prompt: Open all task notes, then compare a single note after starting over. Explore sharing a pending reply and filtered pages.
planning.explanation: Vem compares declared sources across the views that currently need information. Three task-note views can share a cheaper collection read; one view can use a detail read. A second view can join an in-flight fixed representation. A supported filter narrows acquisition, and the runtime follows pages until the actual response establishes completeness. The receipt counts real source calls to the simulated service.

liveness.title: Different fields, different guarantees
liveness.prompt: Go offline, change the service, then reconnect. Keep the reply pending, return an error, or confirm the new title.
liveness.explanation: The real runtime receives an immutable task ID, a title supported by a scoped event channel, and a temperature snapshot. Losing continuity makes the title stale and triggers an unsuccessful targeted read while the simulated service is offline. A service change does not silently update the disconnected view. Reconnecting starts a held check while the old title stays visible. The user can return an error: the title remains last known and the checking indication stops. Retrying and accepting the reply establishes the new title. The ID stays immutable and the old temperature remains a snapshot without automatic polling.
